subject: Agriculture
title: Resistant Varieties
description: A micro-lesson that makes Resistant Varieties usable.

hook.text: Breeding disease resistance into crops is the cheapest, most sustainable disease control. No sprays needed.

buildup.text: Plants have immune systems—they recognize pathogen molecules and activate defense genes.

discovery.text: Breeders screen thousands of plant lines against diseases, selecting those with natural resistance genes.

twist.text: Single-gene resistance typically breaks within 3–5 years as pathogens evolve to overcome it.

climax.text: Stacking multiple resistance genes into one variety makes it harder for pathogens to evolve past all defenses.

punchline.text: One lock is easy to pick. Five locks together buy decades.

quiz.question: Why does single-gene disease resistance often fail within a few years?
options: Pathogens evolve to overcome the single defense

details.summary: Disease and pest-resistant crop varieties are bred to withstand specific pathogens or insects without chemical treatment. This topic covers how resistance is bred into crops, the different types of genetic resistance, and why pests eventually overcome resistant varieties.
details.whyItMatters: Resistant varieties are the most cost-effective and environmentally friendly form of pest management. However, the arms race between breeders and evolving pests means resistance must be continually updated through ongoing breeding programs.
takeaways: Resistant varieties reduce pesticide need and are the cheapest form of pest control
Single-gene resistance is strong but usually overcome by pests within 5-15 years
Gene stacking and quantitative resistance provide more durable but partial protection

faq.question: How are pest-resistant crop varieties developed?
faq.answer: Breeders screen wild relatives and landrace crops for resistance genes, then cross them into commercial varieties through traditional breeding or marker-assisted selection. Modern genomics accelerates identification of resistance genes, and gene editing can introduce resistance more precisely.

faq.question: Why do resistant varieties eventually stop working?
faq.answer: Pests evolve. In large pest populations, rare mutant individuals can overcome the resistance gene. When only resistant plants are grown, these mutant pests have a selective advantage and multiply. Within 5-15 years, the virulent pest strain dominates and the variety loses protection.
